unit_title: How My Body Works and Stays Well
standards: Michigan Health Practice 3: Information and Resource Seeking
Michigan Health Practice 5: Self-Management and Goal Setting
Michigan Health Topic (Grades 3-5): Personal Health and Wellness

prompts.prompt: Explain body systems working together in your own words and give or identify a valid example.

Use a diagram of a general figure or character rather than your own body, a picture sequence, a model, a described demonstration, or a checked source, to show what you learned about germs and how illness spreads.
Apply what you learned about handwashing and respiratory etiquette to a new fictional situation. Show the steps or name the source you relied on.
A made-up character makes an unsafe or unreliable choice involving dental and skin care. Explain what is wrong, correct it, and say why the correction is safer.
Connect body systems working together with checkups and staying well. Explain how the two ideas support or depend on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design a prevention routine that explains what each step protects, why it works, and when adult or professional help is needed.
Name one skill you can now use somewhere else, one way to check your own work, and one question you still have. This is about the skill, not about your private life; nothing private has to be shared.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70-84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery. The transfer item asks about the skill; optional private reflection is separate and is never scored.

accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Choosing an adapted or opt-out path is never scored as a deficit.

standards: Michigan Health Practice 1: Self-Awareness and Analyzing Influences

prompts.prompt: Explain what different foods do for the body in your own words and give or identify a valid example.

Use a diagram of a general figure or character rather than your own body, a picture sequence, a model, a described demonstration, or a checked source, to show what you learned about food allergies and cross-contact safety.
Apply what you learned about media messages about food and bodies to a new fictional situation. Show the steps or name the source you relied on.
A made-up character makes an unsafe or unreliable choice involving building balanced meals and snacks. Explain what is wrong, correct it, and say why the correction is safer.
Connect what different foods do for the body with reading a simple food label. Explain how the two ideas support or depend on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a week of flexible meal, snack, hydration, and movement options with substitutions for allergies, preferences, culture, and budget. No calorie counting, dieting, weight goal, or body measurement is used.
